result:
None of the three solutions is correct, and I did not derive the true minimum k, so my pick is a low-confidence guess.

All three solutions claim that no k exists. Their construction only handles blocks of the form 10^M, …, 10^M + k − 1 with k ≤ 10^224. In that case the digit sum stays at most 2017, below 2025. This is the only part they actually prove, and it covers just small k.

Each solution then waves its hands for larger k ("more advanced constructions", "more elaborate construction"). That step is unjustified and very likely false. For blocks of length about 10^225 or more, the low-order digits can reach any digit sum, so the digit sums cover every residue mod 2025. A finite k therefore very likely exists, and it should be on the order of 10^225.

The "Final answer" lines also disagree with the boxed answers (1, k and 2025), so none of them gives a consistent, valid answer. Solution 1 at least states a definite integer, so I choose it, though it is almost certainly not the true minimum.

CHOICE: 1
